title: 2025 budget adjustments and waste collection changes
subtitle: Also covered: EarlyON lead agency, transit fares, tariff impacts, library review, Seniors' Services settlement, and public health update.
overview: Regional Council finalized adjustments to the 2025 operating budget, including striking a proposed funding reduction for encampment security. Council also approved funding and staffing to prepare for the new curbside waste collection contract in 2026. That vote was split {{vote:m11}}. The costs are to be covered by one-time Blue Box transition revenue and the Waste Management Reserve Fund, with no tax levy impact.

Council chose the YMCA of Three Rivers as the EarlyON Child and Family Centres lead agency for eight years starting January 1, 2026. It also approved lower Affordable Transit Program fares from July 1, 2025, and an extension option for the e-scooter licence agreement with Neuron Mobility. Council directed staff to provide library cost information and arrange an audit-related review at the Library Committee's request.

After a closed session, Council approved a tentative Memorandum of Settlement with Unifor Local 1106 for Seniors' Services staff. A union representing other regional workers told Council it was worried about a strike deadline of March 3. Council received a staff report on the possible effects of US tariffs. The Chair also marked Pink Shirt Day.

decisions.detail: Council amended the 2025 operating budget as set out in the staff report that responded to its earlier budget motion {{vote:m8}}.
Council amended 2025 operating budget lines for supplies, equipment, travel and other items, and struck the proposed funding reduction for encampment security.
Council approved $1.25 million in 2025 prep costs, $1.49 million in 2026 and $452,000 in 2027, and 18 temporary positions for the new collection contract {{vote:m11}}.
Council selected the YMCA of Three Rivers as lead agency for an eight-year term from January 1, 2026, with estimated 2026 funding of $4,329,945.
Council reduced Affordable Transit Program fares from July 1, 2025, and approved an option to extend the Neuron Mobility licence for 2026 to 2029 seasons.

Council directed staff to report three years of library costs and revenues for the townships and to work with the external auditor on a past shared position, with costs capped at $10,000 from the Library budget.
Council approved a tentative Memorandum of Settlement with Unifor Local 1106 covering January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2027.
Council extended the Overlap Associates contract on the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness for one year at $132,960 plus taxes.

debate: On the budget, one councillor said the staff list of proposed cuts resembled an old "Z list" of unpalatable cuts. The councillor supported the motion but called for a more robust budget process so 2026 avoids a similar increase.

Several councillors questioned the travel budget reduction. They had expected it to cover councillors and to cut more. Staff said it applies to staff only, follows the 5% increase limit, and keeps legislated training and site mileage.
A councillor asked about the effect of possible provincial changes to photo radar in school zones. Staff said they had only briefly reviewed a platform and would respond if legislation changes.
A union delegate asked Council to return to the table with the earlier wage offer, saying a reduced offer had damaged trust. The delegate said members did not want a strike on March 3.
A delegate asked Council to review costs of the Partners for Climate Protection program and consider withdrawing. A councillor asked staff for more information by email.
A delegate from a family literacy program said sustainable funding is a challenge because many funders support either children's or adult literacy, not both.
